text: Composite source label: by the 1260s Mongol rule had fragmented into connected but separate khanates. This shape preserves Cliopatria’s aggregate label/extent; it must not be read as proof of uniform central government in 1280. No replacement boundary has been invented.

text: The source can show aggregate imperial extents alongside colonial or dominion records. Overlapping aggregate and component shapes are not additive: summing their areas would double-count land. These shapes do not imply equal political status or identical forms of control.
